Finally, we train a looped Transformer with recurrent KV replay, where only selected recurrence iterations write KV states that later iterations reuse. This trains the model to operate with the same shared KV topology used during inference. We find that looped hybrids require sufficiently frequent attention anchors, with performance depending strongly on the recurrent mixer. For cross-iteration KV sharing, recurrent KV replay allows multiple recurrence iterations to reuse the same KV states while retaining performance close to the full looped Transformer with separate KV caches for each iteration.

papers.title_en: Loop-Count Schedules in Looped Transformers: An Empirical Study
papers.authors: Konstantin Kolokolov
papers.evidence: 研究共享权重循环Transformer中循环次数的训练调度
papers.tldr: 循环Transformer通过共享权重重复同一组层，以参数换计算，但训练中循环次数如何调度尚缺系统认识。作者构建4600万至1.1亿参数的模型阶梯，在每次循环上加入学习式残差门，比较固定两次、1至6均匀采样与2至4采样三种调度。结果显示采样区间下界最具决定性：若区间包含单次循环，门控会收缩到0.1至0.5，额外循环退化为小幅修正。该研究给出了循环次数调度影响循环模型行为的关键经验规律。
papers.abstract_en: Looped transformers apply one block of layers several times with shared weights, trading parameters for repeated computation. We study how the schedule of the loop iteration count R during training determines whether each extra pass acts as a full layer or as a small correction, using a controlled ladder of 46M-110M-parameter models trained on 2B tokens with learned residual gates on every loop pass and three schedules: R fixed to 2, R sampled uniformly from {1,...,6}, and R sampled from {2,3,4}. We find that the lower bound of the sampling range is the decisive choice. If the sampled range includes R=1, so that some training steps run the block only once and compute the loss on that single pass, the gates collapse to 0.1-0.5 and each additional pass becomes a small correction to the first; if the range starts at R=2, so that every training step runs the block at least twice, the gates stay at 0.6-0.9 and each pass keeps the strength of a full layer, while the model can still be run at any R from 2 up to twice the largest trained value with validation loss within a few hundredths of a nat of its best. The {2, 3, 4} schedule gives the best looped model, 2.909 nats against 2.951 for the parameter-matched plain model, and degrades by only 0.038 nats when run at twice its trained depth. We further show that under a fixed R the direction of the residual stream converges geometrically beyond the trained depth while the loss diverges, which refines a recent finding that static-depth training does not converge, and that reusing the first pass's keys and values on later passes costs 0.01-0.03 nats in every regime while making the per-token iteration uniformly contractive and halving the inference cache. The loop recovers about a third of what real depth provides at equal parameters. The code, trained weights, and per-token traces are released.

papers.title_en: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
papers.authors: Xuanlei Zhao, Hailun Xu, Kai Wang, Yang Luo, Yingxuan Ren, Zirui Zhu, Yuxuan Lou, Kun Xu, Yan Wang, Kanchan Sarkar, Yang You
papers.evidence: 在预训练大模型中用循环感知残差迭代共享层块
papers.tldr: 循环 Transformer 通过迭代共享层块在不增加参数的情况下提升计算量与测试时扩展能力，但此前需从零训练且对大模型收益有限。本文提出 LoopRes，基于注意力残差让每个循环层直接关注先前循环的输出，并用可训练的循环感知键区分同层迭代结果。实验表明该方法可将循环转化为对预训练大模型显著且稳定的性能提升，使廉价微调获得接近从头训练的循环收益。
papers.abstract_en: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. Since these outputs are iterates of the same layers and become harder to tell apart, we give each a trainable loop-aware key that encodes its structural identity. Attending to all earlier loops also lets layers skip intermediate ones, so we restrict each layer to a residual window of the latest W loops, forcing every loop to build incrementally on recent ones. Across 6 pretrained LLMs from 3 model families and 9 benchmarks, LoopRes delivers significant and consistent gains: at 2x compute, it improves Qwen3-1.7B-Base by 29.1% over SFT, more than doubling the gain of the state-of-the-art baseline. The gains hold on larger models up to 30B and across all three families. More importantly, from 1.7B to 8B, LoopRes scales more steeply than SFT as compute grows, reaching a higher ceiling while needing less compute on long outputs. These results establish LoopRes as an effective looping approach, delivering both better performance and better test-time scaling.

papers.title_en: Learning from Recurrence: Internalizing Depth-Induced Preferences in Looped Language Models
papers.authors: Hui Chen, Joshua Elsdon, Can Goksen
papers.evidence: 循环语言模型在预测每个词前反复应用同一共享块，并在不同递归深度上训练
papers.tldr: 循环语言模型在预测每个词之前反复应用同一层块，递归深度越高计算越多而参数不变。作者将预训练OLMo-2-1B改造为带共享循环块的模型，并在不同递归深度上继续中期训练。实验发现四遍模型的额外遍数主要在首遍已高排名的词之间重新分配概率，并可用更深层的续写反向训练共享块，为循环模型的深度利用提供了新视角。
papers.abstract_en: A looped language model repeatedly applies the same block to its hidden state before predicting each token. The number of passes is its recurrent depth. Increasing this depth gives the model more computation per token with the same parameters. Can the shared block learn from the predictions it makes at greater depth? Following prior work, we retrofit pretrained OLMo-2-1B with a shared recurrent block and continue mid-training over varying recurrent depths. In the four-pass model, additional passes mainly redistribute probability among tokens that already rank highly after one pass. We use the continuations generated at greater depth to train only the shared block through a single pass, without reference answers or correctness filtering. We call this transfer preference write-back. Write-back further improves one-pass and multi-pass accuracy on most tasks. At their target depths, the updated models outperform a non-recurrent control matched for mid-training data and token budget on all six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with a mean relative gain in accuracy of up to 46.2% across tasks. At four-pass inference, one-pass training outperforms full-depth training on the same targets in the model with input injection. This advantage disappears in the matched model without injection. On GSM8K, using the updated block only on passes two through four recovers nearly the entire four-pass gain, showing that an update learned in one pass can improve later applications of the same block.

papers.title_en: Scaling Looped MoE Language Models under Matched Budgets: Information Flow and Parameter Allocation
papers.authors: Shipeng Bai, Jiayu Qin, Hong Liu, Xili Wang, Jianchao Tan, Jiacheng Li, He Zhang, Yifan Lu, Jiaqi Zhang, Kefeng Zhang, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai
papers.evidence: 在等参数等算力约束下扩展循环Transformer语言模型
papers.tldr: 循环Transformer能将计算深度与参数量解耦，但在等参数、等FLOP约束下如何配置层循环仍缺乏系统设计原则。作者通过门控内循环状态更新与跨阶段残差连接改进信息流，并系统研究循环参数配置。受控实验表明，单次前向核心深度取展开总深度的25%至35%、并把节省的参数重新分配，可在匹配预算下取得更优性能。该工作为循环式大语言模型的架构设计提供了可操作的配置指南。
papers.abstract_en: Looped Transformers decouple computational depth from parameter count, and prior studies have demonstrated promising performance gains with increased computation. However, systematic design principles for configuring these models under strict iso-parameter and iso-FLOP constraints remain scarce. We contribute to this direction by improving information flow in looped models and systematically studying loop parameter configurations. Specifically, we refine this information flow via gated inner-loop state updates and a cross-stage residual connection. Building on this design, controlled studies identify a configuration combining a single-pass Core depth of 25%-35% of the total unrolled depth with reallocating saved parameters into extra routed experts per layer, improving performance at zero extra compute while preserving compatibility with existing training infrastructure. Evaluated after 1T pre-training tokens, our 69B MLA and 51B KDA Mixture-of-Experts models outperform budget-matched non-recurrent baselines by an average of 1.16 and 2.29 percentage points across four benchmarks, respectively. Further reproduction experiments on a common backbone with a 200B-token training budget show that our method achieves lower perplexity than other looped methods. Code for these reproduction experiments is available at https://github.com/lxi01766/Scaling-Looped-MoE-Language-Models-under-Matched-Budgets-Information-Flow-and-Parameter-Allocation.

papers.title_en: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
papers.authors: Lianghui Zhu, Shijie Wang, Xinggang Wang, Jinze Bai, Bo Wang, Xiang Bai
papers.evidence: 面向大模型跨循环复用共享层的循环Transformer
papers.tldr: 循环Transformer依靠复用共享层提升表达能力，却牺牲了推理效率。作者提出混合循环Transformer，用混合循环注意力把键值作为跨深度与跨循环的选择性复用记忆，并设计保留残差流的MoLT-R与从嵌入重启的MoLT-KV两种变体。MoLT-KV去除同位置跨循环依赖，配合循环强制支持并行训练。该工作把循环大模型的表达性与效率前沿向前推进了一步。
papers.abstract_en: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

papers.title_en: Relaxed Recursive Transformers: Effective Parameter Sharing with Layer-wise LoRA
papers.authors: Sangmin Bae, Adam Fisch, Hrayr Harutyunyan, Ziwei Ji, Seungyeon Kim, Tal Schuster
papers.evidence: 将大模型转为单层块循环重复、参数共享的递归Transformer
papers.tldr: 大语言模型部署成本高昂，而现有层绑定式参数共享在现代大模型上效果有限。作者重新审视层绑定，提出把标准预训练Transformer高效初始化为递归Transformer：只保留一个唯一的层块并循环重复多次，同时引入逐层LoRA构成松弛递归Transformer以恢复表达灵活性。实验表明该方法在几乎不损失性能的前提下显著压缩模型规模。其贡献在于为大模型提供了可落地的循环层复用压缩路径。
papers.abstract_en:
Large language models (LLMs) are expensive to deploy. Parameter sharing offers a possible path towards reducing their size and cost, but its effectiveness in modern LLMs remains fairly limited. In this work, we revisit "layer tying" as form of parameter sharing in Transformers, and introduce novel methods for converting existing LLMs into smaller "Recursive Transformers" that share parameters across layers, with minimal loss of performance. Here, our Recursive Transformers are efficiently initialized from standard pretrained Transformers, but only use a single block of unique layers that is then repeated multiple times in a loop. We further improve  performance by introducing Relaxed Recursive Transformers that add flexibility to the layer tying constraint via depth-wise low-rank adaptation (LoRA) modules, yet still preserve the compactness of the overall model. We show that our recursive models (e.g., recursive Gemma 1B) outperform both similar-sized vanilla pretrained models (such as TinyLlama 1.1B and Pythia 1B) and knowledge distillation baselines---and can even recover most of the performance of the original "full-size" model (e.g., Gemma 2B with no shared parameters). Finally, we propose Continuous Depth-wise Batching, a promising new inference paradigm enabled by the Recursive Transformer when paired with early exiting. In a theoretical analysis, we show  that this has the potential to lead to significant (2-3$\times$) gains in inference throughput.

---

papers.title_en: Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation
papers.authors: Sangmin Bae, Yujin Kim, Reza Bayat, Sungnyun Kim, Jiyoun Ha, Tal Schuster, Adam Fisch, Hrayr Harutyunyan, Ziwei Ji, Aaron Courville, Se-Young Yun
papers.evidence: 递归Transformer在递归步骤间复用共享层堆栈
papers.tldr: 扩展语言模型带来高昂的训练与部署开销，已有高效化工作或聚焦参数共享或聚焦自适应计算，难以兼得。作者提出Mixture-of-Recursions框架，在单一递归Transformer中复用共享层堆栈以实现参数效率，同时用轻量路由器为每个词元动态分配不同递归深度。实验表明该设计在保持性能的同时显著减少注意力与计算开销。其贡献在于把循环层复用与自适应计算统一到同一架构中。
papers.abstract_en:
Scaling language models unlocks impressive capabilities, but the accompanying computational and memory demands make both training and deployment expensive. Existing efficiency efforts typically target either parameter sharing or adaptive computation, leaving open the question of how to attain both simultaneously. We introduce Mixture-of-Recursions (MoR), a unified framework that combines the two axes of efficiency inside a single Recursive Transformer. MoR reuses a shared stack of layers across recursion steps to achieve parameter efficiency, while lightweight routers enable adaptive token-level thinking by dynamically assigning different recursion depths to individual tokens. This allows MoR to focus quadratic attention computation only among tokens still active at a given recursion depth, further improving memory access efficiency by selectively caching only their key-value pairs. Beyond these core mechanisms, we also propose a KV sharing variant that reuses KV pairs from the first recursion, specifically designed to further decrease memory footprint. Across model scales ranging from 135M to 1.7B parameters, MoR forms a new Pareto frontier: at equal training FLOPs and smaller model sizes, it significantly lowers validation perplexity and improves few-shot accuracy, while delivering higher throughput compared with vanilla and existing recursive baselines.

---
